text:
alex_sre: Heads-up — planned rolling KV-cache drain in us-west1 to apply hotfix for a prefix-caching regression. Window: Sun Mar 22 02:00-04:00 PDT (UTC 10:00-12:00). Expected: brief increase in first-token latency for cold prefixes (~100–200ms) for ~5–10 minutes per node while caches refill. No data loss expected. Customers with pinned model variants unaffected.

oncall-bot: Scheduled maintenance created: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20260322-kv-drain. Pager policy: page only if error rate > 1% sustained for 5m or 95th token latency > 2s. :spiral_calendar:

liz_ops: TL;DR for customer email? I can draft if we want a single blast. Suggest we explain impact, the window, mitigation, and contact link.

alex_sre: Please do. Also adding fallback plan: we will route traffic to warm pool in us-east1 for heavy-traffic customers during the drain. Canary will run on 10% of nodes first.

mike_eng: Ops runbook snippet I'm using:
```
# drain command
kubectl cordon node/gpu-uw1-04
kubectl drain node/gpu-uw1-04 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
# restart inference-daemon with new kv-fix image
kubectl set image ds/inference-daemon inference-daemon=redwood/inference:kvfix-20260321
```
Monitor: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/kv-cache/us-west1?orgId=1

jordan_support: I'll pre-fill a support template and CS will have the FAQ. Add me to customer notify list for Dedicated accounts.

ops_lead: On-call handoff notes — @alex_sre will be primary until 03:30 PDT, @mike_eng will shadow and take over if any alert escalates. After completion, run validation suite: `make validate-serving` and post results to the thread.

deploy-bot: Deploy started for canary group. Build: kvfix-20260321, sha: abcdef1

alex_sre: Customer email (draft):
"Hi — we're planning a short maintenance window to apply a cache consistency fix in our us-west1 region on Sun Mar 22 02:00-04:00 PDT. You may see a brief increase in latency for some requests while caches re-warm; throughput and correctness will be maintained. If you have latency-sensitive SLAs or a Dedicated deployment, reply to this message and we'll help schedule a targeted migration or standby routing. Full details: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20260322-kv-drain"

liz_ops: Internal statuspage update (short):
"Maintenance: KV cache hotfix rollout in us-west1. Start 02:00 PDT, expected completion by 04:00 PDT. Users may see brief elevated latency as caches repopulate. No data loss."

jordan_support: FAQ snippet:
- Q: Will requests fail? A: No, requests will be served; you may see higher latency for the first requests to a cold prefix.
- Q: Dedicated customers? A: Contact support and we'll arrange isolated maintenance windows.

alex_sre: After we've confirmed canary healthy (10m no errors, 95th < 1s) we proceed to staggered drain of remaining AZs with 15m spacing. If error rate spikes, rollback to previous image and route traffic to us-east1 warm pool.

mike_eng: I'll run the warm-pool prefill 30m before starting and post the prefill completion timestamp.

oncall-bot: Maintenance completed for canary at 02:18 PDT. No errors detected. Moving to AZ-B.

alex_sre: Final check — validation suite passed. `make validate-serving` -> OK. Posting to status page and sending customer email now. Please archive this thread after 24h.

liz_ops: Sending customer blast + updating status page now. :email:

jordan_support: Support ticket template ready and pinned in #support. I'll follow up with the top 5 affected customers (if any). Thanks team.

ops_lead: Thanks all — clean run. Closing out, will file short postmortem note if any customer escalations come in.
